title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: Relations (14) and (17) present PSL(2,Z) and PGL(2,Z), the centre-free groups, whereas the text writes SL(2,Z)' (previous page) and ≃ GL(2,Z) (this page). The prime may denote the quotient by ±1; as written for GL(2,Z) this is an imprecision, since the stack M_{1,1} gives SL/GL with central -1 while the orbifold j-line gives PSL/PGL.

The group T_{0,3} is read as 𝔖_3 × ℤ_12 in the transcription but is presumably 𝔖_3 × ℤ_2 (complex conjugation). If the Z/2 were meant instead as the generic inertia -1, a direct product would be wrong: the quotient of SL(2,Z) by its index-12 free normal subgroup is Z/3 ⋊ Z/4, not S_3 × Z/2.
The existence claim in (17)-(18) is phrased as a desideratum ('on devrait trouver', 'il faudrait'). It is true (classical reflection presentation of PGL(2,Z)), but it is not proved on the page.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful bookkeeping of classical facts: the j-map as the S_3-quotient, PSL(2,Z) = Z/2*Z/3, and PGL(2,Z) as the (2,3,∞) reflection group. It sets compatible generators, oriented versus non-oriented with complex conjugation, in Grothendieck's cartographic-group language. The point of view appears in Esquisse and the cited Teichmüller-tower literature; nothing here appears to be new.
transcription_corrections: The header 'dans Π = 𝔖^+_{0,3}' is an insertion belonging to the first sentence ('trouver dans Π = 𝔖^+_{0,3} des conjugués'), not a separate heading.
The note under (16) most likely reads 'groupe cartographique triangulé non orienté ≃ GL(2,ℤ)' ('triangulaire' crossed out). The symbol in the image looks like 'Cl(2,ℤ)', meaning GL(2,ℤ).
In (16), '𝓜^~_{0,3}' is more likely 'U_{0,3}^{an}' (or U_{0,3} with a decoration), consistent with the previous page.

The garbled sentence before (16) is roughly: 'Si l'on s'inspire d'ailleurs de l'isomorphisme [-plus-] par prolongement (15) et s'obtient : l'isomorphisme' — 'si l'on s'inspire … de l'isomorphisme obtenu par prolongement de (15)'; uncertain.
The equation numbers on this page are written as (14)/(1?), (16), (17), (18) in the image; the numbering restarts relative to the previous page's (14)-(16).
